neighbours.label: a clause boundary (comma, period, 'would') in a narrative of hostile action, just before the retaliation or consequence
fire: The rebels fired on the convoy, and the soldiers answered with rockets.
When the guard raised his sword, the prisoner struck him first.
The ministry warned that the enemy would pay dearly for the raid.
As the pirates boarded the ship, the crew drew their pistols.
He insulted the old warrior. The warrior drew his blade in reply.
The general declared that the invaders would regret their attack.
When the troll swung its club, the knight ducked and slashed back.
The gang set fire to the shop, so the owner called his brothers for revenge.
quiet: The farmers planted the fields, and the children carried water.
When the guest raised her glass, the host smiled warmly.
The ministry announced that the museum would open in May.
As the tourists boarded the ship, the crew handed out maps.
He greeted the old teacher. The teacher shook his hand in reply.
The mayor declared that the festival would begin at noon.
When the baker opened the oven, the bread smelled wonderful.
The family painted the shop, so the owner invited his brothers for dinner.

predictions: Fires weakly at commas and periods in fight or attack narratives before the reaction; quieter in calm narratives with the same punctuation.
notes: Probes were all weak: 'Israel would bear the consequences' 0.13, 'When he tried to do the same, three shots' 0.11, other attack narratives 0.02-0.05; calm controls 0.01-0.03. The label is a guess from the card (combat and confrontation narratives, peaks on ',' and '.'); expected to fail the median.
